observed_problem: The pre-merge acceptance rule had five points. Although repository guidance already told ChatGPT not to stop for ordinary internal work, that behavior was only implicit inside control proportionality and was not independently re-audited. A candidate could therefore retain exactly two formal Human Gates yet still burden production by repeatedly pausing for routine Source Intake, Screening, Evidence, QA, repair, CI retry, or other internally resolvable steps.
expected_behavior: Final candidate review must independently verify stop discipline. After the user supplies the target and requested stopping Gate, ChatGPT continues autonomously through ordinary internal stages, repairs and retries. The only legitimate production interruptions are an actual normal Human Gate, a genuine Owner-level Exception Gate, or unavoidable manual Grok instruction/result transport when Grok execution cannot be crossed directly. Once a Grok result is available in the configured Google Drive run folder, ChatGPT must import it and continue without another routine confirmation.
actual_behavior: The final audit rule is expanded from five to six acceptance points, with AUTONOMOUS PROGRESSION / STOP DISCIPLINE as an independent acceptance condition. Agent/session authority explicitly distinguishes normal autonomous work from Human/Exception Gates and the narrow manual Grok transport exception. Regression tests require the six-point wording and the no-routine-stop contract.

provenance.human_review_reference: Owner instruction 2026-08-22: add an explicit audit point confirming ChatGPT does not stop except at Human Gates or unavoidable manual Grok instruction transport

improvement_action: Make autonomous progression an explicit sixth final-audit point; synchronize repository authority and regression tests so routine internal work cannot be treated as repeated user decision points.
